# Item Faction Overview

by VisionGLLast Updated: October 3, 2026

### Advertisement

This website is supported by ads.

Item Factions are Last Epoch's answer to balancing between players who enjoy trading and those who prefer to find items independently or in smaller groups. You choose your Item Faction based on the playstyle you enjoy the most. The Merchant's Guild lets you trade with other players through an Auction House called the Bazaar. Meanwhile, Circle of Fortune boosts item acquisition through Passive Bonuses and a mechanic called Prophecies, which let you target farm certain types of items.

## The Item Factions

Item Faction Overview
Choosing Circle of Fortune or Merchant's Guild

### Merchant's Guild

Merchant's Guild lets you trade items with other players through an Auction House called the Bazaar. When you join the Merchant's Guild, you immediately gain the ability to purchase and sell all Item Types on the Bazaar. As your Faction Rank with the Merchant's Guild grows, you can purchase different types of loot bags with Gold and Favor, which contain items such as Keys and Crafting Materials.

### Circle of Fortune

Circle of Fortune lets you target farm items through a system called Prophecies, and includes other Passive Bonuses that offer more efficient target farming, increased item quantity, and increased item rarity. The Prophecy system lets you target different types of item rewards by completing certain objectives, such as killing Bosses or various types of enemies. Lenses are another mechanic tied to Circle of Fortune that allow you to modify your Prophecies in different ways.

## Joining an Item Faction

Item Faction Overview
Joining the Merchant's Guild or Circle of Fortune requires the player to reach the Upper District of Maj'Elka in Chapter 9 of the Campaign. Do this by progressing through the main story up to that point, or use a Temporal Sanctum Key and defeat Chronomancer Julra to open a shortcut straight to Chapter 9.

Here, the player interacts with Zerrick, who briefly describes both Item Factions and directs the player to their base of operations. The Merchant's Guild makes their home at the Bazaar, and the Circle of Fortune can be found at the Observatory. You can go to either location and speak with the Faction Leader to join that Item Faction. Merchant's Guild players speak to Nama near the Bazaar waypoint, and Circle of Fortune players speak to Galila inside the Observatory

## Faction Mechanics

Item Faction Overview
Understanding the different Item Faction mechanics, such as the Item Faction Panel, Rank and Reputation, Favor, Faction Vendors, and Rank Requirements, helps you get the most out of what they have to offer.

### Item Faction Panel

The Item Faction Panel lets you view details of your chosen faction. The default hotkey to open this menu is "Y," or you can open it through the main flyout menu next to the player's Mana Globe.

This panel shows information related to the player's Item Faction, such as:

- Current Amount of Favor
- Current Faction Rank
- Your Progress Toward the Next Faction Rank
- Benefits You Currently Have

There is also a "Leave Faction" button to leave your current faction and a "Visit Observatory/Bazaar" button to fast-travel to your Item Faction's hub area.

The Item Faction Panel

### Item Faction Rank and Reputation

Your Rank with an Item Faction grows over time and determines what benefits you gain from them. You can raise your Rank by gaining Experience through defeating enemies or completing quests. You can also raise it by participating in your Item Faction's core mechanic. For the Merchant's Guild, this means trading in the Bazaar; for Circle of Fortune, this involves completing Prophecies.

Your Faction Rank is never lost or spent and is shared across your account. Characters in different game modes, such as Solo or Standard/Legacy, have separate Faction Ranks.

Both Merchant's Guild and Circle of Fortune have 12 total Ranks.

Faction Reputation Bar and Rank Rewards

### Favor

Favor is the main currency you use when interacting with Faction mechanics. Merchant's Guild and Circle of Fortune offer different ways to spend your favor:

- Merchant's Guild: Use Favor to Purchase or List items on the Bazaar.
- Circle of Fortune: Favor is used automatically to progress and complete Prophecies.
- Both Factions can spend Favor at their Faction Leader to gain Reputation through Item Gambling.

Favor is earned by slaying monsters, with the amount earned varying with the Experience the monster rewards. You can also earn Favor by completing Quests. As you progress further into the game, you acquire larger amounts of Favor.

Favor on the Item Faction Panel

### Faction Vendors

Merchant's Guild and Circle of Fortune both have Faction Vendors. The Faction Leader acts as a vendor that offers Item Gambling. Here, you can select Base Items for purchase and, in return, receive a random quality item matching that base type - including Exalted items. The item Base Types offered through Item Gambling are exclusive to that specific Item Faction. Circle of Fortune members can also collect Lenses from this vendor as their Rank improves, which allows them to modify their Prophecies. Spending Favor in this way increases your Reputation.

The Faction Gambler Window

### Circle of Fortune Rank Requirements

Items acquired through Circle of Fortune mechanics, such as from Prophecies or Rank Passives, have a Rank Requirement attached to them. To equip these items, you must have the Rank listed on the item tooltip. You must also be a member of the Circle of Fortune.

Example of Rank Requirement

## Gifting Faction Items

Item Faction Overview
Items with a Faction Rank tied to them follow the same gifting rules as all other items. To gift an item to another player, they must be present and in your party when the item drops. A Resonance can be used to bypass this rule. Although Rank doesn't impact the ability to gift an item, the receiving player must be the corresponding Rank to equip it.

### Resonances

Resonances are consumables that drop when you play in a party with other players. These items are tied to players who are in the party with you when they drop.

- Resonances let you gift items to players who weren't there when an item dropped. This is useful when one player finds an item that could help another player that they usually party with.

- Resonances are consumed when used.

- Resonances don't let the receiving player equip items with a Faction Rank requirement they don't meet. Example: An Idol with a Circle of Fortune Rank 3 Requirement can't be used unless the receiving player is also Rank 3 with Circle of Fortune.

- This item lets small groups of Circle of Fortune players trade sparingly, even without access to the Bazaar.

Example of Resonance

## Summary

Item Faction Overview
- The Item Faction system impacts how players acquire items.
- The Merchant's Guild is for Trading, and Circle of Fortune is for Solo players.
- Earn Reputation by slaying monsters, completing quests, and spending Favor.
- Earn Favor by slaying monsters and completing quests.
- Items earned through Faction mechanics have a Rank Requirement that must be met in order to equip the item.
